source_text:
Ὅ τε γὰρ Θεὸς Λόγος Θεὸς Λόγος ἐστί, καὶ οὐ σάρξ, κἂν εἰ σάρκα λογικῶς ἐψυχωμένην προσεῖληφε, καὶ ἑνώσει ταύτην φυσικῇ καὶ καθ' ὑπόστασιν ἥνωσεν. Ἥ τε σάρξ, σάρξ ἐστιν ἐψυχωμένη λογικῶς, οὐ Λόγος, καὶ εἰ Θεοῦ Λόγου σὰρξ κατοπτεύεται. Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο οὔτε τὴν αὐτὴν ἀπαραλλάκτως ἀλλήλαις ἐνέργειαν μετὰ τὴν ἕνωσιν τὴν φυσικὴν καὶ ἀσύγχυτον, τουτέστι τὴν ἀληθῆ καὶ καθ' ὑπόστασιν ἔχουσιν· οὐδὲ μίαν καὶ μόνην αὐτῶν τὴν ἐνέργειαν λέγομεν, ἢ οὐσιώδη καὶ φυσικήν, καὶ παντελῶς ἀπαράλλακτον, ἵνα μὴ καὶ εἰς οὐσίαν μίαν, καὶ φύσιν μίαν αὐτὰς συνελάσωμεν, τὴν Ἀκεφάλων παιζομένην παισί, καὶ αὐταῖς ἀναιδῶς προφερομένην αὐτοῖς ῥήμασι σύνθετον.
Ὥσπερ οὖν τὴν ἑκατέρας οὐσίας καὶ φύσεως, ἐξ ὧν ἡμῖν ἀσυγχύτως ἐπὶ Χριστοῦ γέγονεν ἡ ἕνωσις, καὶ τὸν ἕνα Χριστὸν καὶ Υἱὸν ἀπετέλεσεν ὅλον Θεόν, ὅλον τὸν αὐτὸν πιστεύομεν ἄνθρωπον, ἑκατέραν φυσικὴν ὁμολογοῦμεν ἐνέργειαν, ἵνα μὴ τὰς ἀσυγχύτως ἑνωθείσας φύσεις συγχέωμεν, εἴπερ ἐκ τῶν ἐνεργειῶν καὶ μόνων κατὰ τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα δεινοὺς αἱ φύσεις γνωρίζονται. Καὶ τῶν οὐσιῶν ἀεὶ τὸ διάφορον ἐκ τοῦ διαφόρου τῶν ἐνεργειῶν καταλαμβάνεσθαι πέφυκεν· οὕτω καὶ πᾶσαν φωνὴν καὶ ἐνέργειαν, κἂν θεῖά τις ᾖ καὶ οὐράνιος, ἢ ἀνθρωπίνη τε καὶ ἐπίγειος ἐξ ἑνὸς καὶ τοῦ αὐτοῦ προϊέναι Χριστοῦ καὶ Υἱοῦ δογματίζομεν, καὶ τῆς μιᾶς αὐτοῦ συνθέτου καὶ μοναδικῆς ὑποστάσεως, ὡς σεσαρκωμένος τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγος ἐτύγχανεν, ὃ καὶ ἑκατέραν ἀμερίστως καὶ ἀσυγχύτως ἐνέργειαν κατὰ τὰς ἑαυτοῦ φύσεις ἐξ ἑαυτοῦ φυσικῶς προβαλλόμενος· κατὰ μὲν τὴν θείαν αὐτοῦ φύσιν, καθ' ἣν ἦν καὶ τῷ Πατρὶ ὁμοούσιος, τὴν θεϊκὴν καὶ ἀνέκφραστον· κατὰ δὲ τὴν ἀνθρωπίνην, καθ' ἣν καὶ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ἡμῖν ὁ αὐτὸς ὁμοούσιος ἔμεινε, τὴν ἀνθρωπείαν καὶ πρόσγειον· τὴν ἑκάστῃ φύσει φίλην καὶ πρόσφορον· καὶ οὐκ ἐῶν τῶν ὁρώντων τινὰ σκανδαλίζεσθαι, ὡς οὐ Θεὸς ὁ αὐτὸς εἴη, καὶ ἄνθρωπος, ὁ ταῦτα κἀκεῖνα φυσικῶς ἐργαζόμενος.
Διὰ μὲν τοῦ τὸν αὐτὸν ἕνα Χριστὸν καὶ Υἱὸν ἐνεργεῖν τὰ ἑκάτερα, τὴν Νεστορίου μιαρὰν ἐμφράττων ἀπόρροιαν· οὔτε γὰρ δύο κατ' αὐτὸν χριστοὺς καὶ υἱούς, ὡς εἰρήχαμεν, τοὺς ἐνεργοῦντας ταῦτά τε κἀκεῖνα πρεσβεύομεν· διὰ δὲ τοῦ δεικνύναι τὰ ἑκατέρας ἴδια φύσεως ἀσύγχυτα μετὰ τὴν ἕνωσιν μένοντα, καὶ ἑκατέραν τῶν αὐτῶν ὁμοίως προφέρειν ἐνέργειαν, τῷ φυσικῷ λόγῳ γνωριζομένων τῶν φύσεων, καὶ τὴν οἰκείαν φύσιν φυσικῶς ἑρμηνευουσῶν, ἀφ' ἧς ἀμερίστως καὶ φυσικῶς ἐπηγάζετο, καὶ οὐσιωδῶς ἀνεβλύστανε, τὴν Εὐτυχοῦς ἐκτρέπων φιλοσύγχυτον βλάστησιν.
pass_a_gloss: Gloss: 'For God-Word is God-Word and not flesh, even if he assumed flesh rationally ensouled and united it to himself by a natural and hypostatic union. And the flesh is flesh rationally ensouled, not Word, even if it is seen as the flesh of God-Word. Therefore they do not, after the natural unconfused (i.e. true, hypostatic) union, have toward each other the same operation without difference; nor do we say their operation is one and single, essential-and-natural and wholly indistinguishable, lest we force them into one essence and one nature — the composite [operation] played with by the children of the Akephaloi and shamelessly uttered by them in their own words. — Just as [we believe the union] of each essence and nature, from which the unconfused union in Christ has come about for us and made the one Christ and Son wholly God and the same wholly man, so we confess each natural operation, lest we confuse the unconfusedly united natures; since natures are known from operations alone, according to those clever in such things. And the difference of essences is naturally always apprehended from the difference of operations. So also we dogmatize that every voice and operation, whether divine and heavenly or human and earthly, proceeds from the one and same Christ and Son and from his one composite and single hypostasis, as he was the enfleshed Word of God, who also projects from himself naturally each operation indivisibly and unconfusedly according to his own natures: according to the divine nature (in which he was homoousios with the Father), the divine and unutterable; according to the human (in which the same remained homoousios with us men), the human and earthly; the operation friendly and fitting to each nature; and not allowing any of the beholders to be scandalized, as if the worker of these-and-those naturally were not the same God and man. — By the same one Christ and Son working the things of each, blocking the foul efflux of Nestorius (for we do not, as he, honour as workers of these-and-those two christs and sons, as we have said); and by showing that the properties of each nature remain unconfused after the union and that each likewise brings forth its operation — the natures being known by the natural logos, and interpreting their own nature naturally, from which [nature the operation] indivisibly and naturally flowed and essentially welled up — turning aside the confusion-loving sprout of Eutyches.' Key lemmas: ἐνέργεια = operation/activity (not 'energy' in the modern sense); φυσικῇ καὶ καθ' ὑπόστασιν ἕνωσις = natural and hypostatic union; ἀπαραλλάκτως = without any difference, identically; σύνθετον = 'composite' (the Acephali slogan of a single composite operation); προβαλλόμενος = putting/projecting forth; ἀπόρροια = outflow/efflux; βλάστησις = offshoot/sprout.
pass_b_english:
For the God who is the Word remains God the Word, and is not flesh — even though he took flesh endowed with a rational soul, and united it to himself in a union that is natural and according to hypostasis. And the flesh remains flesh endowed with a rational soul, not the Word — even though it is beheld as the flesh of God the Word. For this reason, after their natural and unconfused union — that is, the true union, the union according to hypostasis — the two do not possess an operation identical with one another's beyond all difference; nor do we call their operation one and only, be it essential and natural, and altogether without distinction, lest we also drive them together into one essence and one nature: that 'composite' operation which is the plaything of the children of the Acephali, brought out by them, in their own words, without shame.
Just as, then, we believe in the union of each of the two essences and natures — the essences and natures from which the union in Christ has come to be for us without confusion, and has made him the one Christ and Son, wholly God, and the same one wholly man — so too we confess the natural operation of each, lest we confuse the natures that were united without confusion; since, according to those who are skilled in such matters, natures are known from their operations, and from their operations alone. And the difference between essences is by nature always grasped from the difference between their operations. So too we decree that every utterance and every operation, whether one that is divine and heavenly, or one that is human and earthly, proceeds from the one and the same Christ and Son, and from his one composite and single hypostasis, inasmuch as he was the incarnate Word of God — he who also puts forth from himself, by nature, each of his two operations, without division and without confusion, in keeping with his own natures: in keeping with his divine nature, in which he was also of one essence with the Father, the godlike and ineffable operation; in keeping with his human nature, in which the same one remained of one essence with us human beings, the human and earthly operation, the operation that is proper and fitting to each nature. And he permits none of those who see to be scandalized, as though the one who works these things and those by nature were not himself God, and himself man.
By the very fact that the same one Christ and Son works the things belonging to each nature, he blocks up the foul outflow of Nestorius: for we do not, as Nestorius did, maintain that the ones who work these things and those are two Christs and two Sons, as we have said. And by showing that the properties of each nature remain unconfused after the union, and that each of them likewise brings forth its own operation — the natures being made known by their own natural principle, and each interpreting its own nature naturally, the nature from which the operation issued forth without division and by nature, and welled up in accordance with essence — he turns aside the confusion-loving offshoot of Eutyches.

lemmas.gloss: endowed with a rational soul (of Christ's flesh)
union that is natural and according to hypostasis
indistinguishable, without any difference — the two natures do NOT have an operation identical in this sense
operation/activity proper to a nature — the confession's key term
putting forth, projecting (the incarnate Word puts forth each operation from himself)
outflow, efflux — Nestorius' doctrine pictured as a foul stream to be blocked

choices.why: In the seventh-century debate the word means a nature's proper activity; 'energy' in modern English suggests a substance or power-stuff and misleads. 'Operation' is the term the later council and the scholarship use.
rejected: activity (used in Pass A gloss only)

choices.why: It is the opponents' slogan (one composite operation), quoted to be refused, exactly as Migne's Latin prints it as a term under dispute; the quotes mark it as their word, not Sophronius'.

choices.english: the plaything of the children of the Acephali
choices.why: παιζομένην is a thing toyed with/banded about; the Latin ('quae ab Acephalorum pueris luditur') confirms the sense. 'Children of the Acephali' keeps his contemptuous phrase.

choices.english: according to those who are skilled in such matters
choices.why: δεινός here is 'clever, skilled' (the technical experts — the tradition's logicians), not 'terrible'; the Latin 'qui sunt talia callentes' confirms.

variants: PG variae lectiones col. 3172: n. 18 ἑρμηνεύουσαν for ἑρμηνευουσῶν; n. 19 ἀνεβλάστανε for ἀνεβλύστανε. Printed text followed.
